docs.title: LightAtlas
docs.text: LightAtlas is an autonomous, high-throughput discovery engine and morphological atlas generator for astronomical time-series photometry.

docs.title: Scientific Architecture
docs.text: LightAtlas implements a multi-layer consensus anomaly detection and morphological taxonomy pipeline designed for large sky surveys (e.g. Kepler, TESS, Rubin/LSST).

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Deterministic Synthetic Factory: Reproducible stellar light curve generation with quiet, flare, exoplanet transit, and eclipsing binary profiles.
  • Robust Feature Engineering: 40 specialized time-series features spanning frequency harmonics, autocorrelation width, statistical moments, and physical dip fractions.
  • Deep Learning Anomaly Detection: CPU-optimized 1D convolutional autoencoders and vector-quantized latent representations.
  • Offline HTML Gallery: Fully standalone, zero-network interactive reports with embedded inline SVG curves.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get started with LightAtlas in minutes.

docs.title: Standard Installation
docs.text: pip install lightatlas

docs.title: With PyTorch and Development Extras
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hsynylmz-umhg/lightatlas.git
cd lightatlas
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev,torch]"

docs.title: Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: LightAtlas provides a Typer-powered CLI out of the box:

docs.title: Generate Synthetic Light Curves
docs.text: lightatlas synthesize --n 500 --seed 42 --out synthetic.parquet

docs.title: Run End-to-End Offline Demo
docs.text:
lightatlas demo --n 200 --seed 42 --out-dir runs/demo

This generates: - runs/demo/scores.parquet: Parquet table with anomaly scores and clusters. - runs/demo/gallery.html: Standalone offline visual gallery.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from lightatlas.pipeline import PipelineConfig, run_pipeline

# 1. Define configuration
cfg = PipelineConfig(
    source="synthetic",
    n_curves=250,
    seed=42,
    ae_epochs=5,
    vqvae_epochs=10,
    top_fraction=0.05,
    out_dir=Path("runs/my_experiment"),
)

# 2. Execute pipeline
artifacts = run_pipeline(cfg)

print(f"Scores Parquet: {artifacts['scores']}")
print(f"Visual Gallery: {artifacts['gallery']}")

docs.title: Tutorial 1: Synthetic Light Curve Generation & Anomaly Scoring
docs.text: In this tutorial, we explore how to generate synthetic time-series photometry and score anomalies using the unified pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Generating Deterministic Mixtures
docs.text:
The random_mixture utility creates realistic mixtures of astronomical variable stars and transients:

from lightatlas.synth import random_mixture

# Generate 100 light curves
data = random_mixture(n=100, seed=42, n_points=1024)

print("IDs:", data.ids[:5])
print("Labels:", data.labels[:5])
print("Flux shape:", data.f.shape)

docs.title: 2. Feature Extraction & Anomaly Ranking
docs.text:
from lightatlas.core.features import feature_matrix
from lightatlas.models.isolation import IsolationScorer

# Extract 40 features
X = feature_matrix(data.t, data.f)

# Fit Isolation Forest baseline
scorer = IsolationScorer(contamination=0.05, random_state=42)
scorer.fit(X)
scores = scorer.score(X)

print("Highest anomaly score:", scores.max())

docs.title: Tutorial 2: Processing High-Cadence Survey Photometry (TESS)
docs.text: Learn how to process 2-minute cadence time series from surveys like TESS using the LightAtlas pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Setting Up the Pipeline for TESS
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from lightatlas.pipeline import PipelineConfig, run_pipeline

config = PipelineConfig(
    source="tess",
    n_curves=300,
    n_points=1024,
    seed=123,
    ae_epochs=4,
    vqvae_epochs=8,
    top_fraction=0.03,
    out_dir=Path("runs/tess_sector"),
)

artifacts = run_pipeline(config)
print("Pipeline complete:", artifacts)

docs.title: 2. Inspecting Detected Anomalies
docs.text:
Read the resulting Parquet database with Pandas or PyArrow:

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("runs/tess_sector/scores.parquet")
print(df[["id", "score", "cluster", "rarity"]].head(10))

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Building a Morphological Light Curve Atlas
docs.text: Learn how to group detected anomalies into morphological clusters and generate an interactive, zero-network SVG gallery.

docs.title: 1. Latent Space Clustering & Rarity
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from lightatlas.atlas.cluster import cluster_latent
from lightatlas.atlas.rank import rarity_score

# Latent embeddings Z of shape (N, D)
Z = np.random.randn(200, 16)
clusters = cluster_latent(Z, min_cluster_size=10)
rarity = rarity_score(clusters)

print("Cluster assignments:", np.unique(clusters))
print("Rarity scores:", rarity)

docs.title: 2. Generating the Offline HTML Gallery
docs.text:
The gallery generator writes fully standalone HTML embedding inline SVG curves without external CDN links:

import pandas as pd
from lightatlas.atlas.report import render_gallery

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["STAR_01", "STAR_02"],
        "score": [0.95, 0.88],
        "cluster": [1, -1],
        "f": [np.random.randn(1024), np.random.randn(1024)],
    }
)

render_gallery(df, "atlas_gallery.html")
